newsitem.title: USA: Brady bonds end lower in thin pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Brady bonds end lower in thin pre-holiday trade.

text.p: Emerging debt prices ended the final trading session of the year on a lower note, dragged down by a weaker U.S. Treasury market, in what players deemed as extremely thin trading.
"With an early close today, a full close tommorrow and the end of the calendar year...trading was extremely thin," said one trader.
Following a string of stronger-than-expected U.S. economic reports Treasuries turned sharply lower, traders said.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was quoted off 41/32 at 98-4/32 to yield 6.64 percent at the close.

Market players set out for home early on Tuesday, as the PSA The Bond Market Trade Association recommended an early 1400 EDT/1900 GMT close for the U.S. credit market, ahead of the New Year's Day holiday when markets will remain closed.
Meanwhile, the JP Morgan emerging market bond index, updated after Monday's close of trade, was up nearly 40 percent at 143.73 over the year to December 30.
Russia was the year's biggest gainer, up a spectacular 113.09 percent. South Africa was the year's worst performer rising only 8.63 percent over the same period.
Among brady bond prices, Argentine pars AR4C23=RR were off 5/8 at 63-1/2 bid, while Argentine discounts AR425C23=RR bonds down 1/4 at 77 bid, traders said.
Brazil "C" bonds BRD8D14=RR were down a full point at 73-5/8, Venezuelan Pars VZ675C20=RR were off 1/2 at 76-3/8 bid and Mexico Pars MX625L19=RR were off 1/2 at 73-1/4 bid.
Russia's dollar Vnesh RUVNUSLNS=RR was quoted off 3/8 at 79-3/8 bid.
Peru Citi PEFLG91=RR bonds remained unchanged at 116 bid amid the continuing hostage crisis, traders said.

As the year comes to an end, still 83 hostages remain captive in Peru as rebels belonging to the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement continue their two-week hostage siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
